alice: Heads-up — hit a weird case with streaming responses in the py-sdk. When an async generator is cancelled (client stops iteration), the on_close callback runs twice and the socket stays open on linux. Repro in sample-app.
ben: can you paste a minimal repro?
alice: sure, here's the essence:
```
async def stream_tokens(client):
    try:
        async for chunk in client.stream(...):
            yield chunk
    finally:
        await client._on_close()  # we call cleanup here
```
If the caller cancels the async for, the finally runs and the SDK runtime also triggers its weakref finalizer -> double-run.
carol: looks like we have two cleanup paths: explicit finally + weakref.finalize in StreamWrapper. If both call the same cleanup routine it's not idempotent right now.
sam_devex: is this happening only with async streams or also with the sync iterator? which python-sdk version?
alice: async only. repro on python-sdk 0.8.1 and nightly. Sync iterator path currently doesn't use the weakref finalizer.
michael: I suspect the typing/contract change we made for iterator finalizers caused this. We switched return types in the stubs from AsyncIterator[str] to AsyncIterator[Token] and added a wrapper that attaches a finalizer. That wrapper doesn't mark the cleanup as done.
ben: quick fix idea: centralize cleanup into _close_stream() and set a flag _closed = True; make on_close a no-op if _closed. Also consider dropping the weakref finalizer if the generator already has an explicit finally.
sam_devex: agreed. Also add a small unit test covering double-finalize and a mypy stub test to ensure types still align.
alice: opened a tiny PR with the patch and a unit test: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py/pull/1234 (WIP)
ci-bot: Pull request 1234 opened by alice: automated tests queued.
carol: test suggestion: run `pytest tests/stream_teardown.py::test_double_finalize --maxfail=1 -q` — the failing log looks like:
```
E       AssertionError: socket still open after generator finalizer ran twice
E       socket fd=45 state=ESTABLISHED
```
ben: i'll take ownership of the PR, do the idempotency change + update docstring explaining why we used weakref originally.
sam_devex: can we also update the typed stubs under py-sdk/stubs/ to keep AsyncIterator[Token] and add a comment for maintainers so future refactors don't reintroduce this?
michael: yep i'll add a tiny typing note in the PR.
alice: thanks! this is causing flaky CI for sample-app streaming demos in the onboarding tutorial, so would appreciate a quick patch.
ben: aiming to push fix + tests by EOD, will ping here when merged.
sam_devex: thanks all — after merge, can someone add a short note to docs/devex/streaming-edgecases.md so onboarding doesn't hit this? :thumbsup:
michael: :thumbsup:
